Daejeon :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
From the 1980s, multiple national administrative functions were moved from Seoul to Daejeon, most of which are now located in the [Government Complex](/wiki/Government_Complex,_Daejeon "Government Complex, Daejeon"), resulting in another population increase.[[11]](#cite_note-11) It was elevated to the status of [metropolitan city](/wiki/Metropolitan_cities_of_South_Korea "Metropolitan cities of South Korea") in 1989.[[12]](#cite_note-dbpia.co.kr-12)[[13]](#cite_note-MW-13) The city was a sub host for the [1986 Asian Games](/wiki/1986_Asian_Games "1986 Asian Games"), hosted the [Expo '93](/wiki/Expo_%2793 "Expo '93"), the 2000 [International Mathematical Olympiad](/wiki/International_Mathematical_Olympiad "International Mathematical Olympiad") and will be the main host city of the [2027 Summer World University Games](/wiki/2027_Summer_World_University_Games "2027 Summer World University Games").

Daejeon is situated in a lowland valley with three major rivers, all of them eventually flowing into the [Yellow Sea](/wiki/Yellow_Sea "Yellow Sea") by way of the Geum River. The city is surrounded by several small mountains, and is located approximately 170 km (106 mi) south of [Seoul](/wiki/Seoul "Seoul") and 290 km (180 mi) north of [Busan](/wiki/Busan "Busan"), and 70 km (43 mi) east of the Yellow Sea.[[14]](#cite_note-14) It experiences a [monsoon](/wiki/Monsoon "Monsoon")-influenced, four-season climate with wet, hot summers and drier, cold winters.[[15]](#cite_note-15)

Daejeon is bordered to the east by [Boeun County](/wiki/Boeun_County "Boeun County") and [Okcheon County](/wiki/Okcheon_County "Okcheon County") in [North Chungcheong Province](/wiki/North_Chungcheong_Province "North Chungcheong Province"), to the west by [Gongju](/wiki/Gongju "Gongju") and [Gyeryong](/wiki/Gyeryong "Gyeryong") in [South Chungcheong Province](/wiki/South_Chungcheong_Province "South Chungcheong Province"), to the south by [Geumsan County](/wiki/Geumsan_County "Geumsan County") and [Nonsan](/wiki/Nonsan "Nonsan") in South Chungcheong Province, and to the north by [Sejong City](/wiki/Sejong_City "Sejong City") and [Cheongju](/wiki/Cheongju "Cheongju")

The office was reinstated in the [fourth Constitution](/wiki/Constitution_of_China "Constitution of China"), adopted by the 5th Session of the 5th NPC in 1982.[[22]](#cite_note-:2-24) In the 1982 Constitution, the party developed policy while the state executed it, and the president was conceived of as a ceremonial and replacement figure with a role similar to that of equivalent of figurehead presidents in parliamentary republics. Actual state power was vested in the general secretary of the Communist Party, the premier, and the chairman of the Central Military Commission. As part of the effort to prevent another leader from rising above the party as Mao had done, all four posts were intended to be held by separate people. The president therefore performed ceremonial duties such as greeting foreign dignitaries and signing the appointment of embassy staff, and did not intervene in the affairs of the State Council or the party. The constitution also mandated term limits for the office, stipulating the president and vice president could not serve more than two consecutive terms.[[24]](#cite_note-ksn-26) The title of the office ([Chinese](/wiki/Simplified_Chinese_characters "Simplified Chinese characters"): 国家主席; [pinyin](/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin"): *Guójiā Zhǔxí*), which literally translates to "state chairman", was unchanged in the Chinese text, but a new English translation of "President of the People's Republic of China" has been adopted since 1982, instead of "Chairman of the People's Republic of China".[[25]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWong202324-27)

The posts of the premier, president and CCP general secretary were held by different individuals in the 1980s. That said, in reality political power was concentrated on the chairman of the Central Military Commission Deng Xiaoping. He was effectively the paramount leader, as he had controlled the Party, government and the military from "behind the scenes" without holding any of the three posts. He served as [Minister of Economics and Finance](/wiki/Ministry_of_Economy_and_Finance_(France) "Ministry of Economy and Finance (France)") under President [François Hollande](/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Hollande "François Hollande") from 2014 to 2016. He worked as a senior civil servant at the [General Inspectorate of Finance](/wiki/Inspection_g%C3%A9n%C3%A9rale_des_finances "Inspection générale des finances") and as an [investment banker](/wiki/Investment_banker "Investment banker") at [Rothschild & Co](/wiki/Rothschild_%26_Co "Rothschild & Co"). Macron was a senior adviser to President Hollande, being appointed as [Élysée](/wiki/%C3%89lys%C3%A9e_Palace "Élysée Palace") deputy secretary-general by Hollande after the [2012 presidential election](/wiki/2012_French_presidential_election "2012 French presidential election"). Sully Prudhomme :: Nobel Prize :: chunk_0003
Main article: [1901 Nobel Prize in Literature](/wiki/1901_Nobel_Prize_in_Literature "1901 Nobel Prize in Literature")

The first writer to receive the [Nobel Prize for Literature](/wiki/Nobel_Prize_for_Literature "Nobel Prize for Literature") (given "in special recognition of his poetic composition, which gives evidence of [lofty idealism](/wiki/Lofty_idealism "Lofty idealism"), artistic perfection and a rare combination of the qualities of both heart and intellect"), he devoted the bulk of the money he received to the creation of a poetry prize awarded by the *[Société des gens de lettres](/wiki/Soci%C3%A9t%C3%A9_des_gens_de_lettres "Société des gens de lettres")*. He also founded, in 1902, the *[Société des poètes français](/wiki/Soci%C3%A9t%C3%A9_des_po%C3%A8tes_fran%C3%A7ais "Société des poètes français")* with [Jose-Maria de Heredia](/wiki/Jose-Maria_de_Heredia "Jose-Maria de Heredia") and [Leon Dierx](/wiki/Leon_Dierx "Leon Dierx").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/SullyPrudhommetomb.JPG/250px-SullyPrudhommetomb.JPG)](/wiki/File:SullyPrudhommetomb.JPG)

Grave of Sully Prudhomme at [Père-Lachaise](/wiki/P%C3%A8re-Lachaise "Père-Lachaise") in Paris

At the end of his life, his poor health (which had troubled him ever since 1870) forced him to live almost as a [recluse](/wiki/Recluse "Recluse") at [Châtenay-Malabry](/wiki/Ch%C3%A2tenay-Malabry "Châtenay-Malabry"), suffering attacks of paralysis while continuing to work on essays. He died suddenly on 6 September 1907, and was buried at [Père-Lachaise](/wiki/P%C3%A8re-Lachaise "Père-Lachaise") in Paris.

The [Commissioner's Trophy](/wiki/Commissioner%27s_Trophy_(MLB) "Commissioner's Trophy (MLB)") is awarded annually to the winning team of the [World Series](/wiki/World_Series "World Series"), the league's championship series that concludes the postseason.

Within each league, the division winners are the 1, 2, and 3-seeds, based on win–loss records. The teams with the first, second, and third best records among non-division winners will be seeded 4, 5, and 6 respectively. Throughout the postseason, home-field advantage is awarded to the team with the higher win-loss record, with tiebreakers being applied if necessary. In the [Wild Card Series](/wiki/Wild_Card_Series "Wild Card Series"), the 3-seed will host the 6-seed, and the 4-seed will host the 5-seed, with the winners advancing to the [Division Series](/wiki/Division_Series "Division Series"). Unlike the [NFL](/wiki/NFL "NFL"), there is no reseeding between each series. In the Division Series, the 1-seed goes up against the 4/5-seed and the 2-seed goes up against the 3/6-seed. The winners of those matches will compete in their respective [League Championship Series](/wiki/League_Championship_Series "League Championship Series") for their [league pennant](/wiki/Pennant_(sports)#Baseball "Pennant (sports)"), and the pennant winners will advance to the World Series.[[154]](#cite_note-156) Since 2017, home-field advantage in the World Series is determined by regular-season records of the two league champions, replacing a system used for the prior 14 seasons where the champion of the league that won the All-Star Game would receive home-field advantage.[[150]](#cite_note-WS_homefield-152)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Jules_rimet_trophy_at_preston_museum.jpg/330px-Jules_rimet_trophy_at_preston_museum.jpg)](/wiki/File:Jules_rimet_trophy_at_preston_museum.jpg)

The Jules Rimet trophy, awarded from 1930 to 1970

From 1930 to 1970, the *[Jules Rimet Trophy](/wiki/Jules_Rimet_Trophy "Jules Rimet Trophy")* was awarded to the World Cup winning team. It was originally simply known as the *World Cup* or *Coupe du Monde*, but in 1946 it was renamed after the FIFA president [Jules Rimet](/wiki/Jules_Rimet "Jules Rimet") who set up the first tournament. In [1970](/wiki/1970_FIFA_World_Cup "1970 FIFA World Cup"), [Brazil](/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team")'s third victory in the tournament entitled them to keep the trophy permanently. However, the trophy was stolen in 1983 and has never been recovered, apparently melted down by the thieves.[[61]](#cite_note-61)

After 1970, a new trophy, known as the FIFA World Cup Trophy, was designed. The experts of FIFA, coming from seven countries, evaluated the 53 presented models, finally opting for the work of the Italian designer [Silvio Gazzaniga](/wiki/Silvio_Gazzaniga "Silvio Gazzaniga"). The new trophy is 36 cm (14.2 in) high, made of solid 18 [carat](/wiki/Carat_(purity) "Carat (purity)") (75%) gold and weighs 6.175 kg (13.6 lb).[[62]](#cite_note-Trophy-62)

The base contains two layers of semi-precious [malachite](/wiki/Malachite "Malachite") while the bottom side of the trophy bears the engraved year and name of each FIFA World Cup winner since [1974](/wiki/1974_FIFA_World_Cup "1974 FIFA World Cup").[[62]](#cite_note-Trophy-62) The description of the trophy by Gazzaniga was: "The lines spring out from the base, rising in spirals, stretching out to receive the world. From the remarkable dynamic tensions of the compact body of the sculpture rise the figures of two athletes at the stirring moment of victory."[[63]](#cite_note-63)
